The bind is NOT config-dependent -- mh.dll loads its transport before it knows which configuration it is in -- so this file gets the identical step. lines.why: INSERTED BY fork F4B, and it is the item's ONE ruled baseline edit -- pre-ruled as a CLASS at F4A, which measured the cost of the DllMain arm as exactly one structural line at this position. mh.dll now LOADS its transport (mh_net.dll) with LoadLibrary + GetProcAddress as the FIRST statement of DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH, so the bind's outcome line is the first thing in mh_net.log -- ahead even of the lane line, because MH_ModuleBind_Early runs before MH_Launch_Init. VERDICT THAT AUTHORISED IT (check_arm_order --compare, a pre-F4B run of the same mode -> this one): 1 structural edit, 0 text changes, and NOTHING ELSE MOVED. It is ONE line and not two on purpose: the loader-order fact (the R2 measurement) is folded into this same line rather than printed separately, so the bound, absent and declined arms are structurally identical and cost one step each.

lines.t: ; [modules] libmh: BOUND at DllMain (under the loader lock) -- <N> exports resolved, init returned <X>, call-through ok; module DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH was AFTER mh.dll's by <N> us (attach_calls=<N> attach_tid=<N>, mh.dll tid=<N>)
lines.why: INSERTED BY fork F4D, and it is the SECOND member of the class F4A pre-ruled at ruling (b): a satellite bound from DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH costs exactly one structural line at the head of the window. This one is libmh.dll -- the 627-TU SPINE, 94.6% of what mh.dll used to be. It sits after mh_net's rather than before it for no deeper reason than that mh_net's line already holds that position in this file; the two modules do not know about each other and neither DllMain does anything, so the order between them is not a contract (mh.c says so). ONE line and not two, for the same reason mh_net's is: the R2 loader-order fact is folded in. VERDICT THAT AUTHORISED IT (check_arm_order --compare, the pre-F4D run of this same mode -> the F4D run): 2 structural edits, 0 text changes, 42 -> 44 lines, and NOTHING ELSE MOVED.

lines.t: ; [modules] mh_harness: BOUND at DllMain (under the loader lock) -- <N> exports resolved, init returned <X>, call-through ok, host=<N>/<N> spine=<N>/<N>; module DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH was AFTER mh.dll's by <N> us (attach_calls=<N> attach_tid=<N>, mh.dll tid=<N>)
lines.why: INSERTED BY fork F4E, and it is the item's ONE ruled baseline edit -- the THIRD member of the class F4A pre-ruled at ruling (b): a satellite bound from DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH costs exactly one structural line at the head of the window. This one is mh_harness.dll, the determinism/replay INSTRUMENT -- seams/harness.cpp, 8.3k lines, which used to be mh.dll's single largest file. VERDICT THAT AUTHORISED IT (check_arm_order --compare, the pre-F4E run of the same mode -> the F4E run): 1 structural edit, 0 text changes, and NOTHING ELSE MOVED -- measured on all four committed templates (brokered 70->71, original 44->45, brokered_nomodule 72->73, config1 40->41). It is ONE line and not two on purpose, the same constraint both sibling binds state: the loader-order fact and the two row counts are folded into this line rather than printed separately, so the bound and absent arms are structurally identical and cost one step each. The row counts (host=27/27 spine=30/30) are the item's own evidence: host rows resolve out of mh.dll and spine rows out of libmh.dll, and `spine=0/30` is Q4's refusal stated in numbers -- configuration (1) with the instrument declining to arm rather than reading invented state. IT GOES LAST OF THE THREE BINDS, and that IS a contract (see mh.c): the instrument is handed libmh's bind verdict as an argument, so it cannot be bound before libmh has been. -- ALT (fork F4E): the same step as read on a lane with NO mh_harness.dll. Absence of the instrument is not a different ARM -- it is the same thirteen shims answering what the un-armed bodies already answered -- so it is an alternative spelling of this step rather than a fifth template. The registered `harness_absent` scenario is the lane that reads it. The `call-through ok` clause is not decoration and is required by tools/check_module_bind.py: GetProcAddress succeeding is not evidence that a CALL across the boundary works, and neither is the module's init returning its ABI (that is a call into the module-level entry, not into the contract). The probe is MH_Harness_WantsPresentTick, chosen for the three reasons MH_Net_IsStarted is one module over -- pure, no side effect, and a KNOWN answer at DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH (0, because load_config has not run).

lines.why: RETARGETED BY fork F4C-GATE (2026-09-13): same three lines, a different manifest. Q7 dropped no_cd_EN from the compile list (reimplemented in seams/standalone.cpp) and the shipped set is now the three EN caphike/relocate manifests; `[config] mode=original` is the configuration in which one of them actually APPLIES, because in brokered their sites sit inside promoted bodies and the C1 interlock refuses (see brokered.json's entries, which are the refusal pair). MEASURED on a STANDARD make_lane lane (see brokered.json's twin entry for the shape): `check_arm_order --compare original_off original_inmem` = 1 structural edit / 0 text changes / 45 -> 48 lines, these three insertions at step #10 and nothing else, and BOTH lanes then PASS against this file; and the same configuration on the rig booted menu -> lobby with all 6 mp_menu_walk captures PASS (the VM's own log carries the APPLIED line). `optional` as before: [patch] inmem ships OFF. THE `alt` SPELLINGS ARE THE MEASUREMENT, not defensiveness: this line reports WHO holds the baked VA, and that is a property of the process rather than of the build. Three were observed on 2026-09-13 -- MEM_MAPPED (the local parity lane), MEM_PRIVATE (a standard local lane with the transport armed) and MEM_IMAGE, where the occupant is mh.focus.exe's own image and the line names it (the rig VM; the path masks to <PATH>). The vocabulary is CLOSED -- the applier prints state from {FREE,COMMIT,RESERVE} and type from {IMAGE,MAPPED,PRIVATE} -- so a fourth spelling is an observation to add here, not a regression. What never varies, and is the point of keeping the step at all, is that the VA is NOT FREE: that is F1E's hard finding, and a run where this line disappeared would mean the baked-VA placement had started succeeding.

lines.t: ; ==== MP transport seams armed (lobby send/recv + in-game lockstep send/recv hooked) ====
lines.why: MOVED HERE BY fork F3B (ruling Q1), and this is the item's ONE ruled reorder. The four transport install_jmps used to run FIRST, ahead of set_owner_table + reimpl_probe_install. They are DETOURS, so G68's order -- owner_table + reimpl_probe -> MH_InMemPatch_Install -> detours -- puts them after the interlock registry and after the patcher, which is where MH_Net_Arm is now called from. The all-or-nothing prologue guard that used to justify the early position is internal to the net arm (do not half-install the TRANSPORT), not a claim on the rest of the DLL. Verdict that authorised the edit: check_arm_order --compare on three lanes (brokered harness-off / harness-on / original) -- 2 structural edits, 0 text changes, same line count, this line and nothing else.

It joins its three siblings here -- [statebind], [hostapi], [libmh_in] -- and it earns its place only after the split: until F4D libmh_set_hook_api was a same-image pointer assignment, so a bound table was correct by construction; now it is one of ~100 GetProcAddress rows, an unbound hook table does NOT abort (absence is a configuration -- libmh/state/hook_api.h), and the failure mode is therefore silent: every [promote] installer refuses and nothing says why. `spine=` is on the line for the same reason -- with no libmh.dll the generated thunks answer zero, so rc=0 unbound=0 would read as a healthy bind of a table that does not exist.
